# Some variety is not generated by its groups with solvable word problem

Not every variety of groups is generated by its finitely generated groups with solvable word problem: there are a fully invariant subgroup $N$ of the free group $F_\infty$ on countably many generators and a word $w \notin N$ such that $f(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism $f : F_\infty \to G$ into every finitely generated group $G$ that satisfies all laws in $N$ and has solvable word problem with respect to some surjection $F_n \to G$. Kleiman answered Kourovka problem 6.17 in the negative.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), *Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook*, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49, Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 6.17 (A. V. Kuznetsov).
- Yu. G. Kleiman, Some questions in the theory of varieties of groups, Math. USSR-Izv. 22 (1984), 33-65, doi:10.1070/IM1984v022n01ABEH001433.
